title: Establishment of Class E Airspace; Columbus, TX
summary: This action proposes to establish Class E airspace at Columbus Community Hospital Heliport, Columbus, TX. The FAA is proposing this action to support new instrument procedures and instrument flight rule (IFR) operations.

title: Amendment of Class E Airspace; Del Rio, TX
summary: This action amends the Class E airspace at Del Rio, TX. This action is the result of a biennial review of the airspace associated with Laughlin Air Force Base (AFB), Del Rio, TX. This proposal also updates the name and geographic coordinates of Laughlin AFB to coincide with the FAA's aeronautical database. This action brings the airspace into compliance with FAA orders and supports instrument flight rule (IFR) procedures and operations.

title: Connect America Fund; A National Broadband Plan for Our Future High-Cost Universal Support, Reforming the High-Cost Program for an All-IP Future, Safeguarding Universal Service Funding Through Effective Applicant Vetting
summary: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC or Commission) initiates a rulemaking to establish a vetting process for applicants for, and other recipients of, certain new funding awards of high-cost Universal Service Fund (USF) support.

title: Amendment of Class D and E Airspace and Removal of Class E Airspace Over Lebanon, NH
summary: This action proposes to amend Class D and Class E airspace over Lebanon, NH. This action would increase the lateral dimensions of the Lebanon, NH, Class D airspace to appropriately contain Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) operations at the Lebanon Municipal Airport. This action would also update verbiage in the Class D airspace legal description to comply with current FAA guidance. This action would also update the geographic coordinates for the airport in both the Class D and Class E5 airspace legal descriptions. This action would also remove the exclusions for adjacent Class E5 airspace from the Lebanon, NH, Class E5 airspace legal description. This action would also remove the Lebanon, NH, Class E4 airspace, which is no longer necessary for IFR operations at the airport.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
Horse Protection Amendments; Extension of Postponement of Regulations
summary: On May 8, 2024, we published a final rule amending the horse protection regulations. The final rule was initially scheduled to go into effect on February 1, 2025, except for Sec. 11.19, which was effective on June 7, 2024. On January 28, 2025, we published a postponement of the effective date of the remaining provisions from February 1, 2025, to April 2, 2025. On March 21, 2025, we published a further delay of the effective date to February 1, 2026, and a request for comment on whether the length of the postponement should be extended. On January 28, 2026, based on developments following the issuance of the March 21, 2025, delay of effective date, we published a document further delaying the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2026. On November 13, 2026, we published a proposed rule to remove parts of the 2024 Horse Protection final rule that were vacated by Court order from the regulations, as well as proposing to withdraw the non-vacated parts and update the regulations. As a consequence, in this document, we are issuing an extension of the postponement of the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2027.

title: Cybersecurity Labeling for Internet of Things
summary: In this document, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (Bureau) of the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) seeks comment on recommendations for the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark (USCTM) program, a voluntary cybersecurity labeling program for wireless consumer Internet of Things (IoT) products. The Bureau seeks comment on the design and placement of the FCC IoT Label, display of product registry information, certification renewal, post-market surveillance, and procedures for complaints, noncompliant products, and program administrators that withdraw or whose authority is terminated. These actions would support the establishment and effective administration of the USCTM program and provide consumers with accessible cybersecurity information about certified IoT products.

title: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) Center for Occupational Robotics Research (CORR); Request for Information
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), in the Department of Health and Human Services, requests public input on research priorities and prevention needs related to humanoid robots in workplaces. Through its Center for Occupational Robotics Research (CORR), NIOSH conducts research and provides scientific leadership to improve the safety, health, and well-being of workers who use, wear, or work near robots. NIOSH seeks information on workplace applications, human-robot interaction, performance measurement and validation, and ways to prevent injuries and illnesses throughout design, deployment, and use. This request is for information-gathering purposes only and does not propose new regulations, requirements, or policies.

title: Certain New Chemicals or Significant New Uses; Statements of Findings-August 2026
summary: The Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) requires EPA to publish in the Federal Register a statement of its findings after its review of certain TSCA submissions when EPA makes a finding that a new chemical substance or significant new use is not likely to present an unreasonable risk of injury to health or the environment. Such statements apply to premanufacture notices (PMNs), microbial commercial activity notices (MCANs), and significant new use notices (SNUNs) submitted to EPA under TSCA. This document presents statements of findings made by EPA on such submissions during the period from August 1, 2026, to August 31, 2026.

title: Privacy Act of 1974; System of Records
summary: Pursuant to the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular No. A-108, the National Labor Relations Board ("NLRB" or "Agency") is rescinding eight existing systems of records notices (SORNs) and modifying five others. The NLRB has identified eight SORNs that duplicate government-wide systems of records or have been superseded by other NLRB-specific systems. Records formerly covered by these SORNs are now maintained as part of corresponding government-wide systems or replacement NLRB systems. Additionally, the NLRB is adding two routine uses to five other systems of records to address breach responses consistent with Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-17-12, Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of Personally Identifiable Information (Jan. 3, 2017).

title: Privacy Act of 1974; System of Records
summary: Pursuant to the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular No. A-108, the National Labor Relations Board ("NLRB" or "Agency") proposes to establish a new system of records: NLRB-38, Reasonable Accommodation Records. This system will support the Agency's Reasonable Accommodation program. This system of records allows the Agency to collect and maintain records on current and former employees who request or receive reasonable accommodation on the basis of disability and religion under the Agency's Reasonable Accommodation program as required, respectively, by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended, and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act, as amended.

title: Employee or Independent Contractor Status Under the Fair Labor Standards Act, Family and Medical Leave Act, and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act
summary: This final rule rescinds the analysis for determining employee or independent contractor status under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA or Act) set forth in the Department of Labor's (Department) regulations and replaces it with an analysis similar to what it published in a final rule promulgated in 2021, with several modifications and enhancements. In addition, this final rule amends provisions in the Department's regulations implementing the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act (MSPA) to provide that employee or independent contractor status under those laws should be determined using the Department's FLSA analysis, as the FMLA and MSPA both incorporate the FLSA's scope of employment.

title: Endangered Species; Recovery Permit Applications
summary: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (We or Service) invites the public to comment on permit applications to conduct certain activities with listed species under the Endangered Species Act (ESA). With some exceptions, the ESA prohibits activities involving listed species unless the Service issues a federal authorization, such as a permit, to allow for such activities. The ESA also requires the Service to invite public comment and to consider any information received during the public comment period before issuing a permit for any activity otherwise prohibited by the ESA. We invite the public as well as local, State, Tribal, and Federal agencies, to comment on these applications. We will consider all information received during the public comment period before issuing any of the requested permits.
